newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-VOELKER HEADING FOR GOLDEN HAUL.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-VOELKER HEADING FOR GOLDEN HAUL.

text.p: Olympic medallist Sandra Voelker set her sights confidently on a rich gold medal haul with commanding swims in heats at the European sprints and short-course championships on Friday.
Voelker, who collected 12 gold medals at the four editions of the old European sprint championships from 1991 to 1994, set the standard in the women's 50 metres butterfly and 100 freestyle.
The 22-year-old German swept through the 50 butterfly in 27.31 seconds, just 0.06 seconds outside the European record of Inge de Bruijn of the Netherlands.
She returned soon afterwards to lead qualifiers for the afternoon's final in the 100 freestyle, clocking 54.38 with plenty to spare.
Voelker, 100 freestyle silver medallist and 50 freestyle bronze medallist at this year's Atlanta Olympics, is contesting five individual events plus relays.
Her closest rivals in the morning heats were Sweden's Johanna Sjoberg in the 50 butterfly (27.69) and Britain's Susan Rolph in the 100 freestyle (54.77).
Fellow German Sylvia Gerasch made an inauspicious start in her first appearance at an international championships following a two-year suspension for excessive levels of caffeine.
Gerasch, world 100 breaststroke long-course champion in 1986, failed to make the 100 breaststroke final.
The former East German clocked the seventh-fastest time of one minute 10.08 seconds, 0.32 seconds outside the time of the sixth and slowest qualifier, Madelon Baans of the Netherlands.
Ukraine's Svitlana Bondarenko, silver medallist at the 1995 world short-course championships, led the 100 breaststroke qualifiers in 1:08.37.
Poland's Alicja Peczak, who -- like Gerasch -- served a ban after a positive dope test, made the final in 1:09.39.

The first 13 of 38 titles were at stake in the afternoon session in these inaugural European short-course championships, which combine the sprint events with a programme covering all the Olympic distances bar relays.
